name: Gravattack
abilities: Gravikinesis - levitates, hurls, slams or pins targets with hand gestures, and can redirect the pull of gravity itself
Gravity crushing - increases gravity around a target hard enough to crush them (Vilgax Must Croak)
Orbitakinesis - traps objects and people in an orbit around himself at chosen speeds
Gravity force fields - walls, barriers and domes of gravitational energy
Speed reduction - slowed a light-speed Time Beast to a standstill
Planetoid form - retracts limbs into a sphere with boosted gravity powers, self-levitation and flight
Enhanced strength (punched a hole in the ground) and durability (took Fistrick's Class 12 mecha punches)
Space survivability - he is literally a living planetoid
Black hole generation (accidental, in a gravitational deadlock)
weaknesses: Heavy damage to his molten core causes agony and can trigger a meltdown explosion large enough to destroy the area (Food Around the Corner)
Bulky body struggles in tight spaces (While You Were Away)
Sudden changes of mass throw off his orbit (For a Few Brains More)
Cannot stop energy-based attacks with gravity (Fight at the Museum)
Straining against a light-speed object can accidentally spawn a black hole (Let's Do the Time War Again)
summary: A silicon-based living planet with a face on its torso and a lava core, who bends gravity to pin, crush, orbit or levitate anything around him.
traits: Headless - the face is on the torso, with rock teeth and a molten planetary core
Concept name 'Graviton' was rejected for legal reasons
Size drawn inconsistently across episodes (Derrick J. Wyatt admits size-comp problems)
Judged too powerful for the Reboot's Earth-bound villains
Gravity aura was white before turning green from Vilgax Must Croak onward
notableFeats: Defeated Fistrick's armored mech and saved the Megawhatts (A Jolt From the Past)
Defeated General Attea, SixSix, SevenSeven and EightEight at once (Vilgax Must Croak)
Brokered the Appoplexian-Lewodan peace treaty even while the Hulex tried to detonate his core (Food Around the Corner)
Defeated the Rooters (The Rooters of All Evil) and pinned Exo-Skull into the floor (Fight at the Museum)
Chased and trapped a light-speed Time Beast, accidentally opening a black hole (Let's Do the Time War Again)
Got Max and Luhley off the Chimeran Hammer and flew them to Galvan Prime (Malgax Attacks)

notableEpisodes: Let's Do the Time War Again
appearances.designNotes: Large bulky reddish-brown rock body, no head (face and toothy mouth on torso), molten lava core in the centre, three-toed tan feet, black shorts with green stripes and a green/white belt; Omnitrix symbol on forehead.

scoring.rationale: Special 8: gravity control that pinned four bounty hunters at once, crushed the Rooters and stopped a light-speed Time Beast; gravity domes and orbits double as defense. Durability 8 as a living planetoid that survives space and mech blows. Slow, oversized indoors, energy attacks bypass him, and a damaged core can trigger a catastrophic meltdown - hence the penalties.

notes: ultimateFormId left null: Ultimate Gravattack appeared only once and only as Albedo's Negative Ultimate Gravattack (For a Few Brains More); no version of Ben ever used it. Ultimate Gravattack record exists separately (ultimate-gravattack.json) with baseFormId 'gravattack'.
Also used by Albedo (Negative Gravattack, For a Few Brains More) and Bad Ben (And Then There Were None / And Then There Was Ben) - not counted in usedBy.
The Ultimatrix page infers Gravattack was unlocked before Double or Nothing (UA) because Albedo could later use it, but Ben never used it in UA - no UA appearance.
Gravadactyl (Gravattack + Astrodactyl) is a Biomnitrix concept only, never on-screen. Ben 23 counterpart: Orbit-Man.
Matt Wayne: targets hit a structural limit long before fusion, so Gravattack alone cannot create a black hole; the Time War black hole was a deadlock accident.
